subject: URGENT: Dedicated pool headroom exhaustion & elevated 5xxs — FastBank impact
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fastbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-20T19:02:00Z
Subject: Production alert — sustained latency and 503s (FastBank reserved pool)

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a sustained spike in latency and 5xx errors for our production traffic routed to Redwood Dedicated (reservation id: RSRV-9981). Key observations from our side (19:00–19:50 UTC):
- Median p95 latency ~ 820ms, p99 touching ~ 1.4s on text-generation endpoints
- 5xx error rate ~ 2.8% during peak minute windows, mostly HTTP 503 / downstream timeouts
- Effective throughput measured on our side is ~40% below our expected committed throughput under the reservation

This began roughly at 18:45 UTC and hasn't recovered. This is impacting transaction flows for our chat-assist product.

We need an urgent sync and a short bridge to understand whether this is a transient scheduling/backpressure issue or reserved-capacity failures. Please advise immediate mitigation steps we can accept (failover to hosted variant, temporary rate limiting, or other).

Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Operations, FastBank
lena.ortiz@fastbank.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fastbank.com>
Date: 2027-11-20T19:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Production alert — sustained latency and 503s (FastBank reserved pool)

Thanks for the heads up, Lena — we're on it.

Aditya / Dylan — can you take immediate triage on RSRV-9981? Triage checklist:
- Verify dedicated pool utilization and scheduler queue depth (last 60m)
- Look for large-sequence/long-running requests that may be monopolizing GPUs
- Confirm whether autoscale/burst mechanisms attempted and failed
- If we need an immediate customer-facing mitigation, propose: failover to compatible smaller model quantization (if quality acceptable) OR temporary redirect to hosted burst with consent.

I'll open a 30-min bridge (19:15 UTC) and include FastBank. If this is a capacity shortfall we may need Marissa/Grace to OK emergency burst capacity and a one-time credit if SLA impact is real.

Soojin Lee
Account Lead — Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fastbank.com>
Date: 2027-11-20T19:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Production alert — sustained latency and 503s (FastBank reserved pool) — quick findings

Quick notes from infra: attached snapshot with pool metrics.

Findings (18:30–19:20 UTC):
- Dedicated pool node-group "ded-pool-7" at 98% GPU utilization across N=8 instances; scheduler queue depth spiked to ~180 requests, with mean queue time ~650ms
- A recurring nightly batch job from a different tenant submitted long-sequence generation requests just before 18:40 UTC; these requests cause large KV-cache allocations and extended decode loops — they occupy GPU threads for multiple seconds per request and balloon tail latency
- Autoscale tried to add nodes but failed to reach capacity due to simultaneous placement constraints and a transient image-pull slowdown on the nodepool controller (we saw 503s when new nodes were cycled)

Immediate mitigations we can enact in the next 10–20 minutes:
1) Throttle or backpressure the offending tenant's batch job at the scheduler level (we can do this immediately)
2) Enable policy fallback: route non-sensitive FastBank requests to our hosted fallback cluster for up to 30 minutes (requires customer OK)
3) Spin up emergency burst nodes from pooled reserved capacity (cost: estimate ~$9k–$14k/hr depending on GPU mix) — needs exec approval for spend and a one-time network permission to attach nodes to RSRV-9981

I'll attach metrics: pool-metrics-11pm.png.

Attaching quick playbook: proposed-fallback-plan.pdf (includes client-visible messaging & rollback).

Aditya Rao
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

[attachment: pool-metrics-11pm.png (image), proposed-fallback-plan.pdf (pdf)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fastbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-20T19:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Production alert — sustained latency and 503s (FastBank reserved pool) — immediate steps

Lena — thank you for the traces. Short plan of action we will execute now (pending your OK for #2):
1) We will throttle the noisy tenant batch job at the scheduler level immediately (in progress — ETA ~5 min)
2) With your permission, we can failover non-sensitive calls to our hosted fallback for up to 30 minutes while we stabilize (we will not move any PII or requests flagged by your data-class rules). Please reply with a one-line OK if acceptable.
3) We're proposing to spin up emergency burst nodes if throttling does not bring latency down within 15 minutes. This is a short-lived, high-cost operation and will only be used if necessary.

We will join a bridge at 19:15 UTC (invitation sent).

Soojin

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-20T20:02:00Z
Subject: Exec sync: FastBank reserved throughput shortfall — approval for emergency burst?

Grace / Dylan — FYI and requesting approval for an emergency burst spend if throttling doesn't restore commitments within 15m. Context: FastBank (DB-00421) is hitting 5xxs and throughput shortfall on their reserved pool RSRV-9981. Triage indicates cross-tenant long-sequence batch jobs monopolized GPUs and autoscale did not land quickly due to an image-pull slowdown in nodepool controller.

Recommendation and ask:
- Approve spinning up emergency burst nodes attached to the customer's reservation (estimate $12k/hr). We'll only use until queue depth drops below safe thresholds.
- Approve offering a one-time credit equivalent to two hours of committed throughput if SLA impact confirmed (we will coordinate final amount with RevOps).

If you authorize, we'll proceed with the burst and concurrent customer failover (non-sensitive traffic) to eliminate customer-visible errors. Need an OK within 10 minutes to avoid escalation to the COO.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fastbank.com>, Marco Silva <procurement@fastbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-20T22:05:00Z
Subject: Resolved: temporary mitigation applied and next steps (FastBank)

Lena / Marco — closing note from today's bridge. Summary of what we did and next steps: 
- At ~19:10 UTC we throttled the noisy batch job; queue depth reduced from ~180 to ~25 within 8 minutes
- We pre-authorized a small emergency burst (Marissa approved) but did not need to attach nodes after throttling brought latency down
- We enabled a short, customer-approved routing rule for non-sensitive calls to our hosted fallback for 22 minutes while KV caches warmed on the dedicated pool
- Result: p99 latency dropped from ~1.4s to ~380ms and 5xxs returned to baseline (<0.1%) by 19:30 UTC

Action items:
- Aditya/Dylan: run a root-cause postmortem with scheduler logs and nodepool image-pull traces (INF-987) — due EOD tomorrow
- Customer: confirm whether you'd like an automated scheduler-level rate cap for cross-tenant batch windows (we can propose policy values)
- RevOps / CS: finalize goodwill credit if SLA impact confirmed; I'm tagging DB-00421.

Thanks for patience and speedy coordination — please ping me if you see any regression.

Soojin Lee
Account Lead — Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
